jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Jordan governs AI through cabinet-approved policy and soft law led by the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship (MoDEE); there is no AI-specific law. The Jordan AI Policy 2020 (Cabinet Decision No. 659) created a National Ministerial Committee for AI and called for an ethics charter, a sandbox and legal review, and the AI Strategy and Implementation Plan 2023–2027 turns this into 68 projects across priority sectors. The National AI Code of Ethics (2022), which the Cabinet circulated to all government bodies for compliance, is the main responsible-AI instrument. Binding obligations come from the Personal Data Protection Law No. 24 of 2023 (in force March 2024), which covers profiling, and, for banks, the Central Bank of Jordan's AI Framework (July 2025). The Digital Transformation Strategy 2026–2028 makes data and AI a core axis of government digitalisation.

narrative.review_notes: Deep review completed on 6 October 2026. Documents were read from the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship and the Central Bank of Jordan. The official gazette copy of the Personal Data Protection Law and the Legislation and Opinion Bureau's search could not be read; the gazette index confirmed the publication issue. Official sources disagree on the date the Cabinet approved the AI Policy; the date in the Arabic text is recorded. The national cybersecurity centre, telecom regulator, standards body, procurement department and health and education ministries were searched, and no AI-specific instruments were found.

instruments.summary: Jordan's first AI policy, setting the government's direction for AI across economic sectors under five pillars: governance, legislative and regulatory environment, digital infrastructure, business and investment environment, and capacity building. It creates a National Ministerial Committee for AI chaired by the Minister of Digital Economy, requires MoDEE to report annually and review the policy at least every four years, and calls for a national AI ethics charter, a regulatory sandbox and a review of government procurement rules to ease AI adoption.

instruments.summary: Five-year national AI strategy with five objectives: building AI skills, encouraging AI research, improving the AI investment and entrepreneurship environment, ensuring a legislative and regulatory environment for safe AI deployment, and applying AI tools to raise public-sector and priority-sector efficiency. Its implementation plan lists 68 projects across sectors such as government services, health, education, energy, water, agriculture, transport, finance and cybersecurity. Implementation is supervised by the National Council for Entrepreneurship and a MoDEE strategy unit, with a steering committee of government, private-sector and academic representatives.

instruments.summary: Bilingual (Arabic/English) code issued under the AI Policy 2020 setting ethical principles for the responsible use of AI: humanity and society, inclusiveness and justice, privacy and data, transparency, responsibility and accountability, reliability, integrity and non-fakeness, and environmental sustainability (green AI). It also sets principles for virtual environments and the metaverse and for AI research ethics. It addresses developers, users, operators and investors in the public and private sectors; government bodies were directed by the Cabinet to comply with it.

instruments.summary: Jordan's general data protection law, binding on controllers and processors of personal data inside and outside the Kingdom. It requires prior consent or another legal basis for processing, defines profiling as automated processing to identify a person's trends, preferences or behaviour, and gives data subjects rights including to object to processing and profiling that is unnecessary, excessive or discriminatory. It creates a Personal Data Protection Council and a regulatory unit in MoDEE, and gave existing processors one year after entry into force to comply.

instruments.current_status: Version 1.0 dated July 2025 on the cover; hosted in CBJ's FinCert storage area. The document does not state its own legal force or an effective date. Recorded as mandatory in scope: the text uses "must" for CBJ-regulated banks.
instruments.summary: Central Bank framework for AI used by CBJ-regulated banking institutions, whether developed in-house, procured or outsourced. It sets expectations on AI governance and oversight with a risk-based approach, ethical principles (fairness, explainability, bias mitigation) and customers' right to opt out of automated decisions where appropriate, data privacy and quality, secure development with validation, testing, monitoring and human oversight, AI incident response and business continuity, and third-party risk management.

instruments.official_title: Regulatory Sandbox Framework (FinTech and Innovation Regulatory Sandbox – JoRegBox)
instruments.current_status: Technology-neutral: covers all innovative digital financial solutions; AI is not named explicitly. Recorded because it is the only operating regulatory sandbox in Jordan and AI-based financial solutions fall within its scope of 'innovative digital solutions'.
instruments.summary: Sets the rules of the Central Bank's FinTech and Innovation Regulatory Sandbox: objectives, principles, eligible applicants (licensed banks, fintech startups inside or outside Jordan, university- and government-owned fintechs), eligible activities (banking, insurance, payments, lending, RegTech, SupTech, RiskTech), admission criteria and the stages of testing, normally up to six months. It is technology-neutral and does not refer to AI specifically.

instruments.summary: National digital strategy for 2026–2028 that builds on the 2021–2025 strategy and lists 'leveraging data, artificial intelligence and advanced technologies' as a core axis. It plans AI use in government services, including AI agents for real-time interactive support to users, and an initiative to raise AI awareness among 15,000 government employees, alongside digital infrastructure, digital trust, privacy and skills programmes.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Searched MoDEE, Official Gazette index, lob.gov.jo, NCSC, TRC, JSMO, CBJ, Government Procurement Department, Ministries of Health and Education and the Tawasal consultation portal in Arabic and English. No AI-specific law, public-sector AI rules beyond the strategy and code, AI procurement guidance, NCSC AI security guidance, transparency/algorithm register, national AI standard adoption (e.g. ISO/IEC 42001), government-published AI readiness index, generative-AI-specific guidance or AI treaty signature was found. UNESCO's Recommendation is held in data/regional/UNESCO.json. Technical review notes: Deep review 2026-10-06. Sources read directly: modee.gov.jo PDFs (AI Policy 2020 EN, AI Strategy 2023–2027 AR/EN, Code of Ethics bilingual, draft charter, PDPL official translation and 2025 presentation, DTS 2021–2025 and 2026–2028) and cbj.gov.jo PDFs (AI Framework, Sandbox Framework). modee.gov.jo list pages paginate through ASP.NET postbacks, so only the first page of 'Legislation and policies' could be read automatically; documents were located through the ministry AI page and search. The Official Gazette PDF for Law 24/2023 on doc.pm.gov.jo (DocuWare) returned 'resource removed' to automated reading; the gazette index page for issue 5881 was read. lob.gov.jo (Legislation and Opinion Bureau) search is script-driven and was not usable. Official sources disagree on the date of Cabinet Decision 659 approving the AI Policy (Arabic charter: 20/12/2020; English charter: 20 Feb 2020; Strategy: 20/12/2022); the Arabic date is recorded. No dated official page gives the Cabinet approval date of the AI Strategy. The CBJ sandbox is technology-neutral (recorded with that caveat). Out of scope and not recorded: Electronic Transactions (amendment) Law No. 3 of 2026 (no AI provisions found), MoDEE information-security and social-media policies, Digital Inclusion Policy 2025. Sweep: no AI law, AI bill or AI-specific regulation found by 2026-10-06; no NCSC, TRC, JSMO, procurement, health or education AI instruments found.
